items.rationale: The frame sustained theft damage, so §§ 7.1.1(b) and 7.1.9 cover a pre-loss-equivalent replacement. The €229 gross benchmark is reduced to €142.06 by the shared €500 mobility limit (€500/€806).
The brakes sustained theft damage and are covered at the pre-loss specification under §§ 7.1.1(b) and 7.1.9. The €140 gross benchmark is reduced to €86.85 by the rateable mobility limit.

Under § 4.2.3, the tracker must itself have been taken and not recovered, or damaged. It worked during recovery, and no separate loss or damage is established; €18.61 is conditional on proof of covered damage (€30 × €500/€806).
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.5 exclude servicing an unaffected bicycle. The positive figure is a hypothetical service price only.
Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude additional protective equipment and accessories without a demonstrated loss of the originals. The positive figure is a hypothetical gross price for both items.

Section 7.1.7(f) covers necessary carriage for the damaged bicycle or its repair parts, but § 7.1.10 excludes carriage attributable to elective work. The €26 benchmark becomes €16.13 after rateable allocation.

Sections 7.1.8(f)–(g) and 7.1.10 require a distinct, necessary attendance attributable to the covered repair; the generic line does not establish one. If supported, a €30 gross allowance would be about €18.61 at the estimated allocation rate.

Section 7.1.7(c) covers fitting and testing the replacement frame and brakes, but not assembly for the unaffected bicycle or new accessories. The €113 benchmark becomes €70.10 under the shared mobility limit.

Section 7.1.7(e) covers consumables used in the repair, but § 7.1.10 requires a link to covered work that this generic entry does not establish. A €7 supported charge would be about €4.34 at the estimated allocation rate.

Section 7.1.7(d) allows apprentice labour, but § 7.1.10 requires proof that this hour served the theft repair and was not already included in assembly. A €35 gross hour would be about €21.71 at the estimated allocation rate.

Sections 7.1.7(d) and 7.1.8(g) allow distinct repair labour, not labour already included in assembly or used on elective work. A separately supported €39 hour would be about €24.19 at the estimated allocation rate.
Section 5.2.2(a) expressly covers the initial attendance needed to release the bicycle. The €32 gross benchmark becomes €19.85 under the shared mobility limit.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers cutting and removing the lock to free the bicycle. The €108 gross estimate for both units becomes €67.00 under the shared mobility limit.

Sections 5.2.2(a) and 7.1.8(f) cover a further visit only if required for recovery, and the description does not show why it was needed. A €30 gross attendance would be about €18.61 at the estimated allocation rate if necessity were shown.

items.description: Mandatory impound release and storage fee
items.rationale: Section 5.2.2(c) covers the yard's unavoidable third-party release charge. The stated €100 plus 19% VAT is €119 gross, reduced to €73.82 by the shared €500 mobility limit; the €1,000 recovery cap does not bind.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d) exclude claim processing; this is distinct from the mandatory yard release charge. The positive figure is a hypothetical fee only.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers necessary release labour at every grade, but §§ 7.1.8(g) and 7.1.10 require this hour to be separately supported rather than included in lock cutting. A €35 gross hour would be about €21.71 at the estimated allocation rate.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers skilled release labour if it is distinct from the separately billed cutting operation. The €39 gross benchmark becomes €24.19 under the shared mobility limit.
